newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-PANEL SET TO STUDY DODGERS' RETURN TO BROOKLYN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-PANEL SET TO STUDY DODGERS' RETURN TO BROOKLYN.

text.p: Three New York politicians Thursday appointed a panel to try to do what most every Brooklynite dreams about -- bring the Dodgers back to Brooklyn.

The panel was expected to formulate a business deal to present to the O'Malley family, who announced in January they were selling the Los Angeles Dodgers 40 years after moving the team out of Brooklyn.

Few people with connections to Brooklyn have forgiven the loss of the Dodgers following the 1957 season. Fans of the beloved team rate the late Walter O'Malley just below Hitler and Stalin as great villains of the 20th century.

"The Yankees belong in the Bronx, the Mets belong in Queens and the Dodgers belong in Brooklyn," New York Governor George Pataki said from Brooklyn Borough Hall, while the Dodgers' 1955 World Series pennant was displayed in the background.

Pataki, New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani and Brooklyn Borough President Howard Golden appointed the six-member panel, which includes Roger Kahn, author of "The Boys of Summer", an unofficial history of the Brooklyn Dodgers, and former New York Governor Hugh Carey.
Golden admitted the attempt to lure the Dodgers back east was a long shot. But he said he had already been approached by individuals interested in buying the team and bringing it home.

Some sites for a new Brooklyn stadium have already been considered, Golden said. He declined to give details. The site of storied Ebbets Field, the Dodgers' former Brooklyn home, was converted to apartment buildings after the team left.
The Los Angeles Dodgers franchise is expected to sell for between $300 million and $500 million according to the club, which declined comment on Thursday's announcement in Brooklyn.
